title: Felicia Hemans: Selected Poems, Letters, Reception Materials
reliability_notes: The first standard scholarly edition of Hemans, combining representative poems with her letters and contemporary critical responses; a selection rather than a complete poetical text, so individual volumes must be checked against the originals.

title: Felicia Hemans: Selected Poems, Prose and Letters
reliability_notes: The widely used teaching text of Hemans, gathering poems, prose and letters with critical apparatus; useful for range and context but, like the Princeton edition, a selection rather than a complete scholarly text of the verse.

title: Letitia Elizabeth Landon: Selected Writings
reliability_notes: The edition that re-established L.E.L. as a subject for scholarly study, drawing poems, sketches and criticism chiefly from the annuals and periodicals; because it selects from magazine appearances it does not replace the collected 1830s volumes.

title: The Early Poems of John Clare, 1804-1822 (2 volumes)
reliability_notes: Part of the Oxford scholarly Clare edition that prints poems in the state of the manuscripts and abandons the conflated 'final text' of earlier editors; it covers only the early poems, so the later work must be sought in the companion Oxford volumes.

title: Zofloya: or, The Moor (Oxford World's Classics)
reliability_notes: The standard student edition of Charlotte Dacre's 1806 gothic novel, with introduction, explanatory notes and contemporary reviews; reprints the first-edition text. An alternative scholarly edition is Adriana Craciun's Broadview Press text, more focused on gender and race.

title: Melmoth the Wanderer (Oxford World's Classics)
reliability_notes: The principal scholarly text of Charles Robert Maturin's 1820 gothic novel, with Douglas Grant's introduction and notes and a new preface by Chris Baldick. The Grant edition first appeared in 1979; the paperback here is the 2008 Oxford World's Classics reissue.

title: Self-Control: A Novel (Chawton House Library: Women's Novels, No. 17)
reliability_notes: The modern scholarly reprint of Mary Brunton's 1811 novel in the Chawton House Library series, with Mandal's critical introduction and explanatory notes; reprinted from the first edition.

title: Discipline: A Novel (Chawton House Library: Women's Novels)
reliability_notes: The first modern scholarly edition of Brunton's 1814 novel, with introduction, explanatory notes and collation against the early editions; the other Brunton novels are separately edited in the same series, so this volume does not cover Self-Control or Emmeline.

title: The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner (Oxford World's Classics)
reliability_notes: The standard scholarly text of James Hogg's 1824 novel, reprinting the double frame narrative with Duncan's introduction, chronology and notes; the go-to edition for its Calvinist and Romantic contexts.

title: Nightmare Abbey (The Cambridge Edition of the Novels of Thomas Love Peacock, volume 7)
reliability_notes: A scholarly volume of the Cambridge Edition of Peacock's novels, edited from the originals with textual notes and apparatus; Joukovsky is the leading editor of Peacock, so this is the authoritative text of the 1818 satire.

title: The Monk (Oxford World's Classics)
reliability_notes: The long-standard student text of M. G. Lewis's 1796 gothic novel, with Anderson's introduction and notes; it prints a lightly modernised and partly abridged version of the three-decker, so quotations of the full original should be checked against the 1796 text.

title: Selected Poems of Thomas Hood
reliability_notes: The first genuinely scholarly selection of Hood's verse, with introduction and notes drawing on his manuscripts and periodical appearance; it is necessarily selective across Hood's many volumes, and his comic prose and Almanac verse remain largely unedited.

title: Plays on the Passions: The 1798 Edition
reliability_notes: A scholarly reprint of Joanna Baillie's founding volume of the 'Series of Plays' (Count Basil, The Tryal and De Monfort) with the 'Introductory Discourse' and Duthie's editing; covers only the first instalment of the projected passion series.

title: Joanna Baillie: A Selection of Poems and Plays
reliability_notes: A scholarly single-volume recovery of Baillie's verse, critical prefaces and selected dramas (De Monfort, Count Basil, The Alienated Manor), edited with introduction and notes; it is a selection, so the full Plays on the Passions still require separate consultation.

title: Adeline Mowbray: or, The Mother and Daughter (Broadview Editions)
reliability_notes: The modern scholarly edition of Amelia Opie's 1804 novel (also published under the title 'The Mother and Daughter'), with introduction and notes situating its Godwinian and evangelical contexts; a single-novel edition rather than a collected set.

title: Memorials of the Life of Amelia Opie, Selected and Arranged from Her Letters, Diaries, and Other Manuscripts
author_or_editor: Amelia Opie (compiled after her death from her own papers)
reliability_notes: The contemporaneous biographical compilation drawn from Opie's letters, diaries and journals shortly after her death, still the principal assembled record of her life and opinions; her circle filtered the Unitarian and anti-Jacobin testimony, and no complete modern scholarly edition of the correspondence exists.

title: Annals of the Parish (The Edinburgh Edition of the Works of John Galt)
reliability_notes: A scholarly volume of the Edinburgh Edition of the Works of John Galt, established from the early texts with Irvine's introduction, textual notes and apparatus; the standard modern reading text of Galt's 1821 novel.

title: The Letters of Robert Bloomfield and His Circle
reliability_notes: A scholarly edition of Bloomfield's correspondence and that of his family and circle, calendared and annotated from the manuscripts; invaluable for his life, publication history and labouring-class networks, though it is letters rather than a critical text of the poems.

title: The Selected Writings of Leigh Hunt (6 volumes)
author_or_editor: Robert Morrison and Michael Eberle-Sinatra (general editors)
reliability_notes: The magisterial scholarly collection of Hunt's journalism, poetry and prose from the Examiner and his other periodicals, edited with introductions and notes; the standard reference text for Hunt, though a selection rather than his complete writings.

title: Memoirs of Modern Philosophers (Broadview Editions)
reliability_notes: The modern scholarly edition of Elizabeth Hamilton's satirical novel of 1800 (the Irish novelist c.1736-1816), with Grogan's introduction and notes identifying its anti-Jacobin and anti-Godwin targets; a single-novel edition.

title: Jack Sheppard (Broadview Editions)
reliability_notes: A scholarly edition of Ainsworth's Newgate romance with introduction, notes and contextual material on its reception and illustrations. Note that the novel first appeared in 1839, so it post-dates the 1789-1832 boundary; useful as the bridge from late-Romantic popular fiction to the Victorian sensation novel.

title: Marriage: A Novel
reliability_notes: Dorothy McMillan's critical text of Susan Ferrier's novel, using as base the 1819 second edition rather than the sentimentalised Victorian fourth edition, with introduction and notes; a single-novel edition, so The Inheritance and Destiny must be sought elsewhere.

title: Sources and Style in Moore's Irish Melodies
reliability_notes: The first full scholarly study of Moore's Irish Melodies, tracing his musical and literary sources; it is a critical monograph rather than a text, so Moore's poems themselves still have to be quoted from the printed editions.

title: The Poetical Works of Thomas Moore
reliability_notes: The standard Oxford collected text of Moore's verse, established by Godley from the author's own revised 'collected by himself' edition; dependable for the received texts of Lalla Rookh and the Irish Melodies, but it pre-dates modern textual scholarship and carries no full apparatus.

title: The Poetical Works of William Roscoe; Published in Honour of the Centenary of His Birthday
reliability_notes: The collected poetical text issued for the centenary of Roscoe's birth and still the usual citation for poems such as 'The Wrongs of Africa'; it has never been superseded by a modern scholarly edition, so its constitution of the text is Victorian rather than editorial.

title: The Digital Mitford: The Mary Russell Mitford Digital Archive
publisher: Penn State Erie, The Behrend College (Mary Russell Mitford Society)
reliability_notes: The first comprehensive born-digital scholarly edition of Mitford's letters, sketches and documents in TEI encoding, built at Penn State Behrend under Elisa Beshero-Bondar; the project began in April 2013 and remains under continuous construction, so texts must be cited with the page date.

title: The Poetical Works of James Montgomery (2 volumes)
publisher: Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, London
reliability_notes: The collected poetical text issued after Montgomery's death in 1854 from the state he himself revised, and still the only comprehensive printed body of his verse; no modern scholarly edition exists, so dating and the separation of the Sheffield Register periodical poems must be checked against the originals.

title: Robert Bloomfield: Selected Poems (revised and enlarged edition)
reliability_notes: The first scholarly edition of Bloomfield's poetry, revised and enlarged from the 1998 Trent Editions text, with textual notes and the posthumous poems; it is a selection rather than a complete works, so The Rim, The Good Natured Man and his later volumes still have to be read in the originals or in the Romantic Circles collected writings.

title: The Poetical Works of Barry Cornwall
reliability_notes: Procter's first collected edition of his poems under the pseudonym Barry Cornwall, the text from which his Romantic-era verse is still cited; it antedates the later 1820s-1850s volumes and no modern scholarly edition of his work has been produced.

title: Translation of the Letters of a Hindoo Rajah (Broadview Editions)
reliability_notes: The scholarly text of Hamilton's 1796 novel with its 'Preliminary Dissertation' fully annotated, the edition on which current postcolonial readings of the book depend; her Instructions to a Daughter, Letters on the Elementary Principles of Taste and the later novels remain unedited in modern form.
